title: Moonwalk
tagline: The King of Pop changes the world one performance at a time.

scenes.text: Gary, Indiana, 1969. A ten-year-old boy steps on stage with four older brothers. He stops the show. In the audience, Motown founder Berry Gordy watches in silence. Then: 'That kid is going to be a star.'

scenes.speaker: Michael Jackson
scenes.text: I watched James Brown's feet. The way they moved — it was like electricity from the earth was going through him. I practiced until my feet could do what his did. And then I made them do something else.

challenge.instruction: Michael Jackson: score from the spot.
challenge.fact: Thriller (1982) has sold an estimated 66–70 million copies worldwide — the best-selling album in history. It produced seven Top 10 singles and won a record eight Grammy Awards in one night.

scenes.text: Thriller — released in 1982 — became the best-selling album of all time. Its 14-minute title-track music video was the first video to transform MTV. The moonwalk, performed live on television in 1983, instantly became the most iconic dance move in history.

scenes.speaker: Michael Jackson
scenes.text: I just wanted to give the audience something they had never seen before. I didn't think about whether it was possible. I thought about what it would look like when I got it right.

challenge.instruction: Michael Jackson: steer the particle onto target.
challenge.fact: Jackson's falsetto vocal style, rhythmic precision, and melodic invention were unprecedented in pop music. His vocal range spanned 4 octaves — from bass to soprano — and he used his voice as a percussive instrument as much as a melodic one.

Jackson's arc — from Off the Wall's sophistication (1979) to Thriller's global domination (1982) to the moonwalk's cultural moment (1983) to Earth Song's social conscience (1995) — spanned every register of popular music. He is the only artist to have debuted a dance move that became a permanent part of world culture.

Michael Jackson: get the story out alive.
challenge.fact: The sliding step had existed in various forms since the 1930s and was used by artists including Cab Calloway, Marcel Marceau, and Jeffrey Daniel. Jackson perfected and popularised it on Motown 25 (March 1983), but he credited James Brown and Fred Astaire as his inspirations — not himself as an inventor.

scenes.text: Mother Teresa and Joël Robuchon are still in the rival's hand; they will come to the board one by one. Follow them, start the Art Critique where they stand, and fight with Kill mode on. A player with no Great People left is out of the game.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 7 · Conquest. Deploy, move to wherever the rival stands, start the Art Critique there, and attack with Kill mode on until the rival has no Great People left.
challenge.fact: With Kill mode on, a beaten card is discarded instead of returning to hand. A player with no Great People left, in hand or on the board, is out, and the last player standing wins. A kill won in a Great Person's own stat also counts towards their achievement.
